models.name: High-Fidelity Threaded Contact Model (HFTC)
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static FEA of plate–screw–bone assembly with helical thread geometry, nonlinear contact with friction at all interfaces, and per-screw axial and shear load sharing under standardized boundary conditions.

models.name: Reduced-Order Fast Plate Model (ROFPM)
models.what_it_computes: Implicit linear FEA of the same construct using beam elements for screws with bonded plate–screw interfaces and homogenized bone blocks, reporting per-screw axial and shear load sharing.

mechanisms.name: Axial compression across a fracture gap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines how much load is borne by each screw versus the plate under compressive loading typical of partial weight bearing, affecting risk of screw loosening and construct settling.

mechanisms.name: Varus bending under eccentrically applied load
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Governs plate span bending and screw bending moments on the medial side, a common failure mode in diaphyseal plating.

mechanisms.name: Axial torsion about the long-bone axis
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Controls inter-fragment rotational stability and screw shear, relevant to gait-induced twisting.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–5 Assurance Grade scale (0: not demonstrated; 5: very high assurance) for each model × mechanism.

findings.mechanism: Axial compression across a fracture gap
spans: Across compression and bending, nearly all controlled quantities from the rigs have counterparts in the HFTC, whereas torsion retains a few unmodeled slivers of fixture compliance that justify a slightly lower rating for that alignment.

In the HFTC, explicit representation was achieved for 43 of 46 geometric and material parameters, including helical thread geometry (pitch 1.25 mm, flank angle 60 degrees), underhead locking thread, and plate hole geometry.

findings.mechanism: Axial compression across a fracture gap
spans: For screw–bone friction, five thread engagement tests in polyurethane foam blocks measured mean peak-to-sustained force ratios consistent with an effective Coulomb friction coefficient of 0.31 (SD 0.04).
Plate–bone sliding tests on epoxy-coated foam coupons under 50–150 N normal force yielded an average coefficient of 0.20 (SD 0.03).
findings.span: For screw–bone friction, five thread engagement tests in polyurethane foam blocks measured mean peak-to-sustained force ratios consistent with an effective Coulomb friction coefficient of 0.31 (SD 0.04).

findings.mechanism: Axial torsion about the long-bone axis
spans: For torsion, the effective rotational stiffness of the collar–block–plate interface was measured across three assemblies as 2.8, 3.1, and 2.9 N·m/deg, mean 3.0 N·m/deg (SD 0.15), and used to inform HFTC boundary conditions.
findings.span: For torsion, the effective rotational stiffness of the collar–block–plate interface was measured across three assemblies as 2.8, 3.1, and 2.9 N·m/deg, mean 3.0 N·m/deg (SD 0.15), and used to inform HFTC boundary conditions.

findings.mechanism: Axial compression across a fracture gap
spans: A flat punch test with Coulomb friction was simulated, and the predicted tangential-to-normal reaction 6 plate screw load sharing ratio was compared to the prescribed friction coefficient across load steps, yielding less than 1.5% deviation at 0.20 friction and less than 2.0% at 0.30 friction.

A thread engagement benchmark used a single screw thread segment pressed into an elastic half-space; contact pressure distributions matched semi-analytical expectations for thread contact with less than 3% difference in peak pressure location.
Patch tests for solid element assemblies confirmed equilibrium transmission across element boundaries with residual force norms below 5×105 of applied load.

findings.mechanism: Axial compression across a fracture gap
spans: In HFTC, tightening the contact penetration tolerance from 0.5% to 0.2% of the local element size altered per-screw axial forces by less than 0.6% in compression and bending and 0.9% in torsion at the target loads.
Changing the friction regularization parameter by ±20% altered per-screw shear forces by less than 1.2%.
findings.span: In HFTC, tightening the contact penetration tolerance from 0.5% to 0.2% of the local element size altered per-screw axial forces by less than 0.6% in compression and bending and 0.9% in torsion at the target loads.

findings.mechanism: Axial compression across a fracture gap
spans: In the simulations, a distributed vertical displacement boundary condition was applied to the proximal block surface to match the applied load history, with the distal block constrained to move only in the axial 7 plate screw load sharing direction via kinematic constraints simulating the linear bearing.
Alignment measurements in the rig revealed a mean load line offset of 0.3 mm (SD 0.1 mm) from the hole row centerline, and the model applied the load along the measured line.
findings.span: In the simulations, a distributed vertical displacement boundary condition was applied to the proximal block surface to match the applied load history, with the distal block constrained to move only in the axial 7 plate screw load sharing direction via kinematic constraints simulating the linear bearing.

findings.mechanism: Varus bending under eccentrically applied load
spans: In the simulations, an equivalent moment was applied either by an offset vertical load (HFTC) or directly as a couple about the global axis (ROFPM).
The bending fixture compliance was measured as 0.12 mm per 100 N at the roller contact and included in HFTC as a spring; ROFPM treated the moment as a pure couple without additional compliance.
findings.span: In the simulations, an equivalent moment was applied either by an offset vertical load (HFTC) or directly as a couple about the global axis (ROFPM).

findings.mechanism: Axial compression across a fracture gap
spans: For the ROFPM, beam bending and axial extension were verified by comparing the tip displacement and reaction forces of a cantilever beam to Euler–Bernoulli solutions for three mesh densities; errors decreased with refinement and were below 0.2% at the operative mesh size (1.5 mm element length).
A plate under uniform tension was verified against Saint-Venant solutions with less than 0.3% discrepancy in reaction forces at the prescribed displacement.
Constraint enforcement at beam–solid couplings was checked by applying a rigid-body rotation to the plate and ensuring that beam ends rotated compatibly within 0.05 degrees.
